[b]Ministry of Foreign Affairs[/b]

[u]Baladullah and Maqamistan Establish Bilateral Cooperation, Discuss Possible New Regional Organization of Islamic Cooperation[/u]

[i]بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم [/i]

A delegation from the Peoples Republic of [nation]Maqamistan[/nation] met with officials today in the Grand Royal Masjids professional suite today, to discuss the establishment of diplomatic relations and bilateral ties in the fields of trade, energy, religious affairs, political cooperation, and laying the groundwork for a revived Organization of Islamic Cooperation. 

In attendance from Maqamistan: President Muhamed Velazquez, prime minister Satanay Pasht, Marco ibn Fadlan, Minister of Foreign Affairs; Fatima al-Haqawi, Minister of Friendship of Peoples; and Abdulaziz Al-Kawthari, the grand mufti of maqamistan.

[quote=lavinsworth_united_islands;60517627][spoiler=[b]The Meeting #1[/b]]

In the middle of pulling a sheet with information from its grey folder, Reuter hears someone clear their throat in front of him. Looking up, a blue and white uniformed guard stands before him with an expectant look. Quickly putting the paper back in its place, he, along with the small group of guards with him are escorted into the chateau.

Walking over its polished wood floors, he takes a second to observe the decor. Its a good way to gauge who youre about to meet. The halls were modest yet somehow rich, decorated with a few paintings and objects here and there, and the main rooms were all open to each other. Along with the large windows, it gave the house a very nice feel, one Reuter hoped would transition into the meeting. 

After being led for a short time, the guard would stop just before the entrance to a small meeting room, with the balcony doors to the room open. Walking in, Reuter would hear the sliding doors of the room close behind him. This was most likely to keep the meeting mostly private, but the paranoia of the revolutionaries had messed with his brain. Even though they had recently appointed him, there was still a little voice in the back of his head telling him that the revolutionaries could turn on a dime against him. He didn't have to worry about that here, though. The meeting would go smoothly as planned and his government would love him for securing a national partner and naval assets. 

A chair could be heard moving on the balcony, and a somewhat older middle aged man appeared from the balcony, wearing what appeared to be a dress uniform. This should be David Witstrom, the Livonian Minister of Defence. Our guest is here! Witstrom yelled over his shoulder to others apparently on the balcony before turning back to Reuter. Come friend, we shall talk over wine. 

Without missing a beat, Witstrom walked off back to the balcony, Reuter following close behind. Two more men were sitting on chairs overlooking the vineyard below, one of them being Wallace H. Achebe, however the other isnt recognizable to him. This man wasnt in the information for the meeting, and that makes him feel uneasy.

You okay? The unnamed man asks, raising an eyebrow at Reuter, interrupting his train of worry. Yes, dont worry for me. He would quickly say before taking a seat. Reaching for the chilled bottle of wine to fill himself a glass, a loud screech breaks the silence as something passes over the chateau. The unknown man speaks again. Airbase is the only downside of this place. Those flyboys keep those HALTR aircraft running constantly as of recent he pauses for a second, glancing at Reuter like he was about to say something he wouldnt want the diplomat to hear. 

Achebe broke the awkward silence. Ah, everyone is here and has a full glass. Now, let's get down to what we are here for. Would you mind informing the others of what business we have together? [/spoiler][/quote]

Reuter takes a sip from his glass and then begins to speak.

"So. Right. Firstly

 I'm sure you got that uh..." message" from my cowker. Fuelenger? Right. I am not sure...Muller would let Fuelenger of all people do that. So I would like to apologize for how...brash he was in that message. Typically, that would have been my department.

Secondly, there are these islands, the Aruelen Islands."

He has one of his aides hand a folder around, which basically contains an analysis of the islands courtesy of the Stase. Detailed maps of likely areas around the islands of high oil concentration, and the potential strategic and operational value of naval and airbases on the islands. And even a potential location for civilian settlements. Also speculating that the islands also likely have oil below them.

"Very oil-rich, strategically positioned, very large set of 3 islands and a few atolls, all uninhabited. Fuelenger wants them. So does Müller. Mostly because of the oil, but also because they could offer the NVA a very valuable base. Obvious problem though. We have no navy at all. And therefore, for now, maintaining access to the islands is going to be really, really difficult. It risks the lives of the troops we plan to deploy there severely should anything occur. That's...where you come in."

He points to the maps that show Livonia's proximity to the islands

"My purpose for being here today is to see what your demands would be for allowing Floueschia access to your waters and air bases to ensure effective operations on the islands. We might also need permission for medical evacuations from time to time. We already have a few offers prepared if you would like to hear them first. But I would like to note, we can't be open about these terms completely. The Radical Republicans would never allow certain terms that we are prepared to concede to, and they might raise hell about it if they don't like the terms or they find out we don't tell them about certain terms when this is submitted to the Staatsrot for voting."

President Achebe nods, thinking over the brochure of an intelligence presentation he now holds. After taking a long sip from his glass, he starts. 

Ill keep it quick and simple, then I'll let my compatriots add their requests. The first term would be that Lavian oil companies be involved in some way. Pay them to build infrastructure or operate your wells, however you wish, they just need to be there somehow. [i][u][b]The Declaration of the United States of Oceanic
[/b][/u]

Following the political transition from the Oceanice Enclave Republic to the United States of Oceanic. The now USO nation has embraced a new vision built upon reforms for economic freedom, conservative values, and hyperdemocratic technocratic principles. The Declaration of the United States of Oceanic is a transformation reforming the state into a free, participatory democracy that rejects authoritarian rule.

Under the leadership of President Ironvisak Willham, the United States of Oceanic seeks unity, reconciliation, and equality between Humans and Non-Humans, aspiring to rebuild a nation that upholds liberty and mutual respect. As part of this transition, the USO aims to establish new diplomatic and economic ties with the United Lavian Republic to turn former adversaries into peaceful allies.

[u][b]The National Broadcast opens with a statement from the President of USO[/b][/u]

People of Oceanic, we have endured the long injustice of authoritarianism and division within our homelands. In the past we faced injustices and conflict that brought our great nation to the brink of collapse. But today, we stand at the dawn of a new era. We have turned away from the failures of the past and now set our sights on a future for peace, liberty, and democracy. This era of stability and renewal shall not seek war, but rather peace through strength, prosperity, and unity. Together, we will rebuild Oceanic for the generations to come.
 President Ironvisak Willham

(Crowd cheers)

[u][b]The Official Declaration Act[/b][/u]

The Declaration of the Enclave Commonwealth establishes the foundational principles of the new republic in representative economic policy, conservative governance, and hyperdemocratic technocratic ideals. The new government focuses on integrating the military, government, society, and economy into a unified framework designed to uphold freedom, meritocracy, and efficiency. The declaration ensured a new constitution bill called Free Techno-Democracy Constitution.

The Free Techno-Democracy Constitution guarantees safeguards against authoritarianism, fascism, socialism, and tyranny, ensuring that no ideology may rise to suppress the free will of the Oceanic people. It declares that all intelligent beings of human and non-human alike possess equal rights to life, liberty, and citizenship within the United States of Oceanic. Any being born within, or legally naturalized under the laws of the USO, shall be recognized as a full citizen. However, the Constitution establishes that executive and legislative leadership positions such as the Presidency and high offices of state shall be reserved for human candidates, while non-human citizens retain full suffrage, including the right to vote and participate in national elections. 

The Constitution declares that technology is allowed for liberty use. Every citizen has the right to access, develop, and utilize technology for personal, commercial, and civic advancement. The state is expressly forbidden from monopolizing or censoring technological innovation. Economic activity within the United States of Oceanic is governed by the principle of capitalism without coercion, ensuring an open-market system free from direct government control. The states role is limited to protecting fair competition, enforcing contracts, and preventing bureaucratic or ideological interference that could obstruct innovation.

The FTDC replaces political privilege with technocratic meritocracy, ensuring that governance is conducted by those chosen for proven skill, expertise, and efficiency rather than party loyalty or lineage. Its hyperdemocratic representation system allows citizens to participate directly in policy decisions through Online Assembly Platforms with secure networks enabling instant national voting and civic engagement. All major legislative, social, and economic reforms require majority approval through this system, creating a direct bridge between the people and the state.

The Constitutions Technonomic Separation Clause establishes a strict boundary between government and private enterprise. The state is prohibited from owning or operating commercial entities except within essential defense, security, and space sectors. Private corporations, cooperatives, and innovators maintain full control over production, trade, and technological development. The government acts solely as a regulator of fairness, never as a competitor. Economic data on national productivity must remain open-source and publicly accessible, ensuring transparency and accountability. This framework focuses on prompting a technocapitalist economy where innovation replaces traditional bureaucracy, and free enterprise is protected as a constitutional right.

To prevent the re-emergence of tyranny, the Constitution embeds strong anti-authoritarian safeguards. Any political movement promoting fascism, socialism, or communism is constitutionally banned. Civil surveillance is heavily restricted and requires judicial oversight. The Council of Free Systems, a non-partisan body of engineers, economists, and philosophers acts as the moral guardian of the Constitution, ensuring that technology serves humanity ethically and that civil liberties remain intact.

The Economic and Technological Charter of the FTDC guarantees the right of every citizen, corporation, and institution to freely invent, manufacture, and distribute technology. It formally recognizes cryptocurrencies, autonomous markets, and artificial intelligences as legal economic entities with limited operational personhood. Environmental preservation is enforced through Environmental Technocracy, requiring all industrial activity to adhere to sustainable development standards defined by the Technocratic Council of Ecology. Academic institutions and research organizations are declared self-governing and immune to political interference, ensuring that scientific progress remains independent. The government of the United States of Oceanic operates under a four tier system by the FTDC. The President of the Republic, elected every six years by popular vote, serves as both head of state and protector of the Constitution. The Technocratic Senate consists of specialists representing major industrial and scientific sectors, ensuring informed policy creation. The House of the People functions as a directly elected legislative assembly, representing the civic will of all districts and communities. Finally, the Supreme Constitutional Tribunal serves as the highest legal authority, overseeing constitutional adherence and mediating disputes between citizens, corporations, and the government.

The Free Techno-Democracy Constitution adheres to technological progress and safeguard of liberty. The Free Techno-Democracy Constitution represents the United States of Oceanics transformation from authoritarian rule into a society by focusing on rational freedom, innovation, and equality.

On the 17th of April, 1953, a man stands impatient. The person he was waiting for was supposed to be here an hour ago, and he is getting nervous. Will this truly succeed? But he wipes doubt from his mind. The incompetence cant go on any longer, he must do this for the good of all. Finally, he hears people remark about vehicles approaching the building. Its them.

Stepping out of the central vehicle, is the man who has been causing such a fuss. King Zidan II, on his way to the central committee in order to pass yet another law, which, in the man's mind, will ruin the nation more than it has already been. Those in Elyser and Vespuria have influenced the king too much, and action must be taken.

As the king and his guards walk up the long staircase, he answers questions from reporters and onlookers the best he can while still making good time to the entrance. Now is the chance, the time to strike. Ripping the ancient pistol from its hiding place inside his coat, the man thrusts his arm outwards towards the king as he looks away, trying to answer some newsman.

He pulls the trigger. The bang is heard from inside the crowd, and people run. The bodyguards quickly huddle around the king, doing their best to identify where the shot was from. But the bullet never reached the king. The ancient pistol had exploded in the assassins hand, as the poor upkeep paired with an overloaded homemade bullet caused the weapon to malfunction catastrophically, mauling his hand and sending shrapnel into his face.

The king is ushered back to his motorcade and is secure for now. The news of such an attempt rocks the nation, and finally breaks the tension that has been building for so long. The majority of the military, under General Abu al-Sharif, would quickly mobilize and center itself around the Eastern Army Command, creating an open rebellion to the kings power, the Sabrati Revolutionary Union.

In the west, where outside influence has been much more, launched into a reactionary revolution. While groups were unorganized, they used meetings and agreements to formalize into one as the Democratic Front.

In the middle of it all, was the king and his family, the House of al-Mahdin. Using their relatively central place in all of this, those still loyal massed around the southern center of the nation to create a bulwark as well as a potential fallback route to the Lavian border.

[spoiler=[b]Another one bites the dust[/b]]
The news of the attempted coup and subsequent unrest would come as no surprise to Hydronias president, Halil Ozhid. To him and his government, this was simply another third world country which had succumb to the consequences of corruption, a situation that had become increasingly common across the world as of late. As such, Halils reaction to civil conflict such as this, in Shamat and abroad had become almost routine. He would first be informed of the specifics of the situation by his intelligence advisors, then he would make a speech addressed to the Sabrati people, the Hydronian people and all other inhabitants of Erene who may be listening. In this speech, he would condemn the actions of the corrupt factions and the commie factions, before expressing his sympathy for the people and Hydronias support for the democratic factions of the war.

One the public arrangements had been made, the real action would begin. Halil would use his presidential powers to authorise an intervention plan. At his command, reconnaissance planes would streak up into the night sky and towards Sabrata, taking images and readings of the landscape below. This data would be brought back to Hydronia and used in bombing operations within 3 days. On the first night, Hydronian bombers would use the camouflage of the dimly light atmosphere to carry out bombing strikes on revolutionary targets. Key roads, oil depots and military installations would be targeted. Carpet bombing would be used to ensure maximum damage, but the conditions of the night could still cause the operation to fail.

In the coming days, reconnaissance planes would once again make rounds above Sabrata, making note of the success of the Hydronian bombings. The newly collected data would once again be utilised in bombing strikes, with each nights attack becoming more successful for Hydronia and more deadly for the revolutionaries.

But whilst this all occurred, Halil would also deploy his diplomatic skills to the conflict. Hydronia must make it look like peace is the ultimate goal, whilst also taking the chance to shine once again on the world stage as a growing superpower and simultaneously eliminate anti-Hydronian, anti-THEP regimes. On the day after the initial strikes on the revolutionaries, Hydronia would reach out diplomatically to the Democratic front. Halil would invite their leader to talks in Hydropolis, so that Hydronian could both gain more info on the faction and provide them with aid, to gain their trust. Equipment, humanitarian supplies, strategists and even troops would all be offered to the Democratic front.

Additionally, Hydronia would reach out to the Lavian government, a close ally of Hydronias, to discuss a joint peacekeeping operation in civilian areas of Sabrata, to help minimise the innocent casualties that would be soon to come.
